label: thm:sobolev
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:sobolev}
Let ${(X,\omega)}$ be a fixed compact K\"ahler manifold. For a K\"ahler form ${\eta}$, set
\[
\color{black}
 V_\eta=\int_X\eta^n,\qquad d\mu_\eta=\frac{\eta^n}{V_\eta},\qquad
 I_\eta=[\eta]\cdot[\omega]^{n-1},\qquad V_\omega=\int_X\omega^n.
\]
Fix ${p>n}$ and constants ${K,c>0}$. Suppose that
\[
\color{black}
 \int_X\left|\log\frac{\eta^n/V_\eta}{\omega^n/V_\omega}\right|^p d\mu_\eta\leq K,
 \qquad \frac{\eta^n/V_\eta}{\omega^n/V_\omega}\geq c.
\]
Then there exist constants ${q=q(n,p)>1}$ and ${C_S>0}$, depending only on the fixed background, ${n,p,K,c}$, and ${q}$, such that, for every ${u\in W^{1,2}(X,\eta)}$,
\[
\color{black}
 \left(\int_X|u-\bar u_\eta|^{2q}d\mu_\eta\right)^{1/q}
 \leq C_S I_\eta\int_X|\nabla u|_\eta^2d\mu_\eta,
 \qquad \bar u_\eta=\int_Xu\,d\mu_\eta.
\]

label: eq:trace-first
title: Proof
body_md:
Integration of \eqref{eq:ht1} gives
$-\underline R=\int_X\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\,d\mu\geq0$.
{Choose source coordinates satisfying} \eqref{eq:estimate-coordinates} {at} $x_0${, and normal target coordinates at} $\Phi(x_0)$, and write
$\omega_Z=\sqrt{-1}h_{\alpha\bar\beta}dw^\alpha\wedge d\bar w^\beta$.
Then
\[
 \chi_{i\bar j}=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}
 h_{\alpha\bar\beta}(\Phi)\Phi_i^\alpha\overline{\Phi_j^\beta},
\qquad \operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi=\sum_{i,\alpha}|\Phi_i^\alpha|^2 =\sum_i\lambda_i.
\]
With $R_{i\bar j k\bar l}=-\partial_k\partial_{\bar l}
g_{\varphi,i\bar j}$ at the normal point, differentiation gives
\begin{align}
 (\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)_k&=\sum_{i,\alpha}\Phi_{ik}^\alpha\overline{\Phi_i^\alpha},
       \label{eq:trace-first}\\
 \Delta_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi
 &=\sum_{i,k,\alpha}|\Phi_{ik}^\alpha|^2
   +\sum_i\lambda_i\operatorname{Ric}(\omega_\varphi)_{i\bar i}-\sum_{i,k,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta}R^{\omega_Z}_{\alpha\bar\beta\gamma\bar\delta}\Phi_i^\alpha\overline{\Phi_i^\beta}\Phi_k^\gamma\overline{\Phi_k^\delta}.
       \label{eq:map-bochner-coordinates}
\end{align}
By Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
\[
|\nabla_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi|_\varphi^2
\leq(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)\sum_{i,k,\alpha}|\Phi_{ik}^\alpha|^2.\]
By \eqref{eq:ht1},
\[\sum_i\lambda_i\operatorname{Ric}(\omega_\varphi)_{i\bar i}=-\sum_i\lambda_i^2-\sum_i\lambda_iF_{i\bar i}.
\]
Choose $K\geq1$ so that the bisectional curvature of $\omega_Z$ is at most
$K-1$. Raising both indices of $\chi$ with $g_\varphi$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht3}
 \Delta_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi
 \geq\sum_{i,k,\alpha}|\Phi_{ik}^\alpha|^2
       -K(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2-\sum_{i,j}\chi^{i\bar j}F_{i\bar j}.
\end{equation}
Here $\chi^{i\bar j}=g_\varphi^{i\bar b}\chi_{a\bar b}
g_\varphi^{a\bar j}$, so $\chi^{i\bar j}=\lambda_i\delta_{ij}$ at
the normal point.

For $0<\delta\leq1$, put $v=\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi+\delta$. Since $v>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht4}
 \Delta_\varphi v\geq\frac{|\nabla_\varphi v|_\varphi^2}{v}
       -Kv^2-\sum_{i,j}\chi^{i\bar j}F_{i\bar j},\qquad
 \Delta_\varphi F=-\underline R+\delta-v.
\end{equation}
The closedness of $\chi$ gives, at the normal point,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht5}
\sum_i\nabla_{\varphi,i}\chi^{i\bar{j}}=\sum_i\nabla_{\varphi,i}\chi_{j\bar i}=\sum_i\nabla_{\varphi,j}\chi_{i\bar i}=v_j.
\end{equation}

Fix $p\geq1$, and choose $b\in \mathbb R$ later. Testing \eqref{eq:ht4} with
$e^{bF}v^{p-1}$,
\begin{align*}
 \int_Xe^{bF}v^{p-1}\Delta_\varphi v\,d\mu
 &=-\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\sum_i\left[
 (p-1)\left|\frac{v_i}{v}\right|^2+b\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)\right]d\mu,\\
 \int_Xe^{bF}v^{p-2}|\nabla_\varphi v|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
&=\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\sum_i\left|\frac{v_i}{v}\right|^2d\mu,\\
 -\int_Xe^{bF}v^{p-1}\chi^{i\bar j}F_{i\bar j}\,d\mu
 &=\operatorname{Re}\int_X
 \nabla_{\varphi,i}(e^{bF}v^{p-1}\chi^{i\bar j})F_{\bar j}\,d\mu.
\end{align*}
Repeated indices in the last line are summed. Expanding its derivative
and using \eqref{eq:ht5} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}
 \nabla_{\varphi,i}(e^{bF}v^{p-1}\chi^{i\bar j})F_{\bar j}\\
 &\quad=e^{bF}v^p\sum_i\left[
 b\frac{\lambda_i}{v}|F_i|^2
 +(p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}
              \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)
 +\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht6}
\begin{split}
 &\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\sum_i\left[
 p\left|\frac{v_i}{v}\right|^2
 +\left((p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}+b+1\right)
             \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)
 +b\frac{\lambda_i}{v}|F_i|^2\right]d\mu\\
 &\hspace{45mm}\leq K\int_Xe^{bF}v^{p+1}\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Testing the equation $\Delta_\varphi F=-\underline{R}+\delta-v$ with $e^{bF}v^p$ similarly gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht7}
\begin{split}
 &\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\sum_i\left[
 p\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)+b|F_i|^2
 \right]d\mu\\
 &\qquad=\int_Xe^{bF}v^{p+1}\,d\mu
       -(-\underline R+\delta)\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

Subtract $\Lambda$ times \eqref{eq:ht7} from \eqref{eq:ht6}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:trace-combination}
\begin{split}
 \int_Xe^{bF}v^p\mathcal Q\,d\mu
 +(\Lambda-K)\int_Xe^{bF}v^{p+1}\,d\mu
 \leq\Lambda(-\underline R+\delta)\int_Xe^{bF}v^p\,d\mu,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal Q=\sum_i\bigg[
 &p\left|\frac{v_i}{v}\right|^2
 +\left((p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}+b+1-\Lambda p\right)
        \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)\\
 &+b\left(\frac{\lambda_i}{v}-\Lambda\right)|F_i|^2\bigg].
\end{split}
\]
We seek $\Lambda>K$ and $\mathcal Q\geq0$. At the endpoint
$\lambda_i/v=1$, requiring the summand to be
$p|v_i/v-\alpha F_i|^2$ gives
\[
 \begin{cases}
 p+b-\Lambda p=-2p\alpha,\\
 b(1-\Lambda)=p\alpha^2.
 \end{cases}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 (\Lambda-1-\alpha)^2=0,
 \qquad \Lambda=\alpha+1,\quad b=-p\alpha.
\]
For these choices, set $u=e^{-\alpha F}v$. Then
\[
 (\log u)_i=\frac{v_i}{v}-\alpha F_i,
 \qquad 0\leq\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\leq1,
\]
and the coefficients of the remaining terms satisfy
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}+b+1-\Lambda p
 &=-2p\alpha-(p-1)\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right),\\
 b\left(\frac{\lambda_i}{v}-\Lambda\right)
 &=p\alpha^2+p\alpha\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution, followed by $v_i/v=(\log u)_i+\alpha F_i$, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal Q
 &=\sum_i p\left|\frac{v_i}{v}-\alpha F_i\right|^2
 +\sum_i\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right)
 \left[-(p-1)\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)
          +p\alpha|F_i|^2\right]\\
 &=\sum_i p|(\log u)_i|^2
 +\sum_i\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right)
 \left[-(p-1)\operatorname{Re}((\log u)_iF_{\bar i})
          +\alpha|F_i|^2\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
For each $i$, the last bracket equals
\[
 \alpha\left|F_i-\frac{p-1}{2\alpha}(\log u)_i\right|^2
 -\frac{(p-1)^2}{4\alpha}|(\log u)_i|^2.
\]
Hence one gets the complete square identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht8}
\begin{split}
 \mathcal Q
 ={}&\sum_i\alpha\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right)
       \left|F_i-\frac{p-1}{2\alpha}(\log u)_i\right|^2\\
 &+\sum_i\left[p-\frac{(p-1)^2}{4\alpha}
                  \left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right)\right]
                  |(\log u)_i|^2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Choose
\[
 \alpha=K+p,\qquad \Lambda-K=p+1,\qquad
 p-\frac{(p-1)^2}{4\alpha}\left(1-\frac{\lambda_i}{v}\right)
 \geq\frac p2.
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:trace-combination} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht9}
\begin{split}
 &\frac p2\int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^p
                   |\nabla_\varphi\log u|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
 +(p+1)\int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^{p+1}\,d\mu\\
 &\qquad\leq(\alpha+1)(-\underline R+\delta)
                       \int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^p\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

H\"older's inequality gives
\[
 \int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^p\,d\mu
 \leq\left(\int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^{p+1}\,d\mu\right)^{p/(p+1)}
      \left(\int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}\,d\mu\right)^{1/(p+1)}.
\]
Dropping the first nonnegative term in \eqref{eq:ht9} yields
\[
 \int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}v^{p+1}\,d\mu
 \leq\left(\frac{(\alpha+1)(-\underline R+\delta)}{p+1}\right)^{p+1}
       \int_Xe^{-p\alpha F}\,d\mu.
\]
Since $\mu(X)=1$, multiplying by $e^{p\alpha\sup F}$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ht10}
 \int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi+\delta)^{p+1}\,d\mu
 \leq\left(\frac{(\alpha+1)(-\underline R+\delta)}{p+1}\right)^{p+1}
       e^{p\alpha\operatorname{osc}F},\qquad \alpha=K+p.
\end{equation}
Let $\delta\downarrow0$. This proves \eqref{eq:ht2} for $p\geq2$;
for $1\leq p<2$, use $\|\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\|_p\leq
\|\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\|_2$.

label: eq:gradient-bochner
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $w=|\nabla_\varphi F|_\varphi^2$. The Bochner formula gives 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gradient-bochner}
 \Delta_\varphi w
 =\sum_{i,j}(|F_{ij}|^2+|F_{i\bar j}|^2)-2\operatorname{Re}\sum_i(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)_iF_{\bar i}-\sum_i\lambda_i|F_i|^2
 -\sum_{i,j}F_{i\bar j}F_jF_{\bar i}.
\end{equation}
Direct computation gives
\[w_i=\sum_j(F_{ji}F_{\bar j}+F_jF_{i\bar j}),\]
 \[e^{-bF}\Delta_\varphi e^{bF}=b(-\underline R-\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)+b^2w,\]
 \[2e^{-bF}\operatorname{Re}\sum_i(e^{bF})_iw_{\bar i}=2b\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}F_{ij}F_{\bar i}F_{\bar j}
   +2b\sum_{i,j}F_{i\bar j}F_jF_{\bar i},\]
\[ \sum_{i,j}|F_{ij}|^2
+2b\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}F_{ij}F_{\bar i}F_{\bar j}+b^2w^2=\sum_{i,j}|F_{ij}+bF_iF_j|^2.
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{split}
 e^{-bF}\Delta_\varphi(e^{bF}w)
 =&\sum_{i,j}|F_{ij}+bF_iF_j|^2+\sum_{i,j}|F_{,i\bar j}|^2+(2b-1)\sum_{i,j}F_{i\bar j}F_jF_{\bar i}-2\operatorname{Re}\sum_i(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)_iF_{\bar i}\\
 &-\sum_i\lambda_i|F_i|^2+b(-\underline R-\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)w.
\end{split}
\]
The mixed Hessian has no sign; its coefficient vanishes for
$b=\frac12$. This is \cite[equations~(4.3)--(4.4)]{CC17}, with
reference Ricci form $-\chi$. Set
\[
 u=1+e^{F/2}|\nabla_\varphi F|_\varphi^2.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gradient-weighted-exact}
\begin{split}
 \Delta_\varphi u
 =&e^{F/2}\sum_{i,j}\left(|F_{ij}+\tfrac12F_iF_j|^2+|F_{i\bar j}|^2\right)-2e^{F/2}\operatorname{Re}\sum_i(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)_iF_{\bar i}-e^{F/2}\sum_i\lambda_i|F_i|^2\\
 &+\tfrac12(-\underline R-\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)(u-1).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since $0\leq\lambda_i\leq\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi$, dropping the Hessian
squares gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-18c}
 \Delta_\varphi u \geq-2e^{F/2}\operatorname{Re}\langle\nabla_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi,\nabla_\varphi F\rangle_\varphi
 -\left(\tfrac12\underline R+\tfrac32\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\right)(u-1).
\end{equation}

For $p\geq2$, testing \eqref{eq:c-18c} with $u^{p-1}$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gradient-tested}
\begin{split}
 &(p-1)\int_Xu^{p-2}|\nabla_\varphi u|_\varphi^2\,d\mu\\
 &\quad\leq2\int_Xe^{F/2}u^{p-1}\operatorname{Re}\langle\nabla_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi,\nabla_\varphi F\rangle_\varphi\,d\mu\\
&\qquad+\int_X\left(\tfrac12\underline R+\tfrac32\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\right)
                      (u-1)u^{p-1}\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
For the first integral on the right,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gradient-q-parts}
\begin{split}
 &2\int_Xe^{F/2}u^{p-1}\operatorname{Re}\langle\nabla_\varphi\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi,\nabla_\varphi F\rangle_\varphi\,d\mu\\
 &\quad=-2\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)e^{F/2}u^{p-1}
                      (-\underline R-\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)\,d\mu\\
 &\qquad-\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)(u-1)u^{p-1}\,d\mu\\
 &\qquad-2(p-1)\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)e^{F/2}u^{p-2}\operatorname{Re}\langle\nabla_\varphi u,\nabla_\varphi F\rangle_\varphi\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Because $e^{F/2}|\nabla_\varphi F|_\varphi
=e^{F/4}\sqrt{u-1}\leq C\sqrt u$, Young's inequality gives
\[
\begin{split}
 &2(p-1)\left|\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)e^{F/2}u^{p-2}
 \operatorname{Re}\langle\nabla_\varphi u,\nabla_\varphi F\rangle_\varphi\,d\mu\right|\\
 &\quad\leq\frac{p-1}{2}\int_Xu^{p-2}|\nabla_\varphi u|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
       +C(p-1)\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2u^{p-1}\,d\mu.
\end{split}
\]
The terms without $\nabla_\varphi u$ combine to
\[
\begin{split}
 &2\underline R\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)e^{F/2}u^{p-1}\,d\mu
 +2\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2e^{F/2}u^{p-1}\,d\mu\\
 &\quad+\frac12\int_X(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)(u-1)u^{p-1}\,d\mu
 +\frac{\underline R}{2}\int_X(u-1)u^{p-1}\,d\mu\\
 &\qquad\leq C\int_X\bigl(1+(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2\bigr)u^p\,d\mu,
\end{split}
\]
using $u\geq1$.
Absorbing the gradient term and using
$|\nabla_\varphi u^{p/2}|_\varphi^2
=\frac{p^2}{4}u^{p-2}|\nabla_\varphi u|_\varphi^2$ yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-18d}
 \int_X|\nabla_\varphi u^{p/2}|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
 \leq Cp^2\int_X\bigl(1+(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2\bigr)u^p\,d\mu.
\end{equation}


Let $\theta=q/[r(q-1)]\in(0,1)$, where $q>1$. H\"older and interpolation inequality give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:iteration-interpolation}
\begin{split}
 \int_X\bigl(1+(\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)^2\bigr)u^p\,d\mu
 &\leq C\|u^{p/2}\|_{L^{2r/(r-1)}}^2
 \leq C\|u^{p/2}\|_{L^{2q}}^{2\theta}\|u^{p/2}\|_{L^2}^{2(1-\theta)}\\
 &\leq\tau\|u^{p/2}\|_{L^{2q}}^2
       +C\tau^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}\|u^{p/2}\|_{L^2}^2,
 \qquad 0<\tau\leq1.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Apply the uniform Sobolev inequality~\ref{thm:sobolev} to $u^{p/2}$. 
Choosing $\tau=(2Cp^2)^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq:iteration-interpolation}
and absorbing half the left side gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:iteration-step}
 \|u\|_{L^{pq}}\leq\bigl(Cp^{2/(1-\theta)}\bigr)^{1/p}\|u\|_{L^p},
 \qquad p\geq2.
\end{equation}
For $p_j=2q^j$, both $\sum_jp_j^{-1}$ and
$\sum_jp_j^{-1}\log p_j$ converge. Iteration and interpolation yield
\[
 \|u\|_{L^\infty}\leq C\|u\|_{L^2}
 \leq C\|u\|_{L^\infty}^{1/2}\|u\|_{L^1}^{1/2},
 \qquad \|u\|_{L^\infty}\leq C^2\|u\|_{L^1}.
\]
Finally, by \eqref{eq:ht1},
\[
 \int_Xwd\mu
 =-\int_XF(-\underline R-\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)d\mu
 \leq2|\underline R|\|F\|_{L^\infty},
 \qquad \|u\|_{L^1}\leq1+e^{\|F\|_{L^\infty}/2}\int_Xwd\mu\leq C.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:c-18b}.

head: environment

label: eq:q1
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $v=1+\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi$. Taking $\delta=1$, $b=0$ in
\eqref{eq:ht6} gives, for $p\geq2$,
\[
 \int_Xv^p\sum_i\left[
 p\left|\frac{v_i}{v}\right|^2+
 \left((p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}+1\right)
       \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)\right]d\mu
 \leq K\int_Xv^{p+1}\,d\mu.
\]
Since $0\leq\lambda_i/v\leq1$,
\[
 \left|\sum_i\left((p-1)\frac{\lambda_i}{v}+1\right)
       \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{v_i}{v}F_{\bar i}\right)\right|
 \leq p\frac{|\nabla_\varphi v|_\varphi}{v}|\nabla_\varphi F|_\varphi
 \leq\frac p2\frac{|\nabla_\varphi v|_\varphi^2}{v^2}+Cp.
\]
Absorption gives
\[
 \frac p2\int_Xv^{p-2}|\nabla_\varphi v|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
 \leq K\int_Xv^{p+1}\,d\mu+Cp\int_Xv^p\,d\mu,
\]
and hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q1}
 \int_X|\nabla_\varphi v^{p/2}|_\varphi^2\,d\mu
 \leq Cp^2\int_X(1+\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi)v^p\,d\mu.
\end{equation}
For fixed $r>q/(q-1)$, the coefficient $1+\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi$ has a
uniform $L^r$ bound. The interpolation and iteration in
\eqref{eq:iteration-interpolation}--\eqref{eq:iteration-step} therefore give
\[
 \|1+\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\|_{L^\infty}
 \leq C\|1+\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\|_{L^2}\leq C'.
\]
Finally, $\lambda_i\leq\sum_j\lambda_j=\operatorname{tr}_\varphi\chi\leq C'$,
so $\chi\leq C'\omega_\varphi$.

label: lem:energy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:energy}
The functions $F_\varepsilon$, $\varphi_\varepsilon$, have uniformly bounded normalized Dirichlet energy:
\[
\int_X |\nabla F_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\,d\mu_\varepsilon+\int_X |\nabla \varphi_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\,d\mu_\varepsilon\le C.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$\chi\ge 0$ gives
\[
-\underline R_\varepsilon=\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\,d\mu_\varepsilon\ge0.
\]
Note that  $\underline R_\varepsilon\to-m$. Integration by parts yields
\[
\int_X|\nabla F_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\,d\mu_\varepsilon
=-\int_XF_\varepsilon(-\underline R_\varepsilon-\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi)\,d\mu_\varepsilon
\le2|\underline R_\varepsilon|\|F_\varepsilon\|_\infty.
\]
Likewise,
\[
\Delta_{\omega_\varepsilon}\varphi_\varepsilon=n-\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi_\varepsilon,
\qquad
\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi_\varepsilon\,d\mu_\varepsilon=n,
\]
where the last identity follows from $[\chi_\varepsilon]=[\omega_\varepsilon]$. Both $\chi_\varepsilon$ and $\omega_\varepsilon$ are positive. Thus
\[
\int_X|\nabla\varphi_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\,d\mu_\varepsilon\le2n\|\varphi_\varepsilon\|_\infty.
\]

label: lem:compactness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:compactness}
Suppose
\[
 \|u_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty}\leq C,\qquad
 \int_X|\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\,d\mu_\varepsilon\leq C.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{item:lem-compactness-1} $\|u_\varepsilon\|_{W^{1,1}(X,{\omega})}\leq C$. Hence every sequence has a subsequence converging in every finite
$L^p(X,\Omega)$.
\item\label{item:lem-compactness-2} For any compact subset $K\Subset Y^\circ$, put
\[
 \bar u_\varepsilon(y)=V_F^{-1}\int_{X_y}u_\varepsilon{\omega_y}^d.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
 \int_{f^{-1}(K)}|\nabla_Vu_\varepsilon|_{{\omega_y}}\Omega
 &\leq C_K\sqrt\varepsilon,\\
 \int_{f^{-1}(K)}|u_\varepsilon-f^*\bar u_\varepsilon|\Omega
 &\leq C_K\sqrt\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Here $\nabla_V u$ is the covariant derivative in the fiber direction. 
Hence every limit is constant on almost every smooth connected fiber.
For $d=0$, the fibers on $Y^\circ$ are points and this last assertion
is automatic.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
1. By Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
\[
 |\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{{\omega}}^2
 \leq|\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2
                 \operatorname{tr}_{{\omega}}\omega_\varepsilon.
\]
Since $\|F_\varepsilon\|_\infty\le C$, $\mu_\varepsilon, \Omega, {\omega}^n$ are all equivalent,
\begin{align*}
\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{{\omega}}\omega_\varepsilon\,\Omega
 &\leq Cn\int_X\omega_\varepsilon\wedge{\omega}^{n-1}
 =Cn(2\pi c_1(K_X)+\varepsilon [{\omega}])\cdot [{\omega}]^{n-1}\leq C,\\
 \int_X|\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{{\omega}}\Omega
 &\leq C\left(\int_X|\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2d\mu_\varepsilon\right)^{1/2}
       \left(\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{{\omega}}\omega_\varepsilon\,\Omega\right)^{1/2}\leq C.
\end{align*}
Rellich compactness gives $h_{\varepsilon_j}\to h$ in $L^1$; then
\[
 \|h_{\varepsilon_j}-h\|_{L^p}^p
 \leq(2C)^{p-1}\|h_{\varepsilon_j}-h\|_{L^1}\longrightarrow0.
\]

2. Take $K\Subset K'\Subset Y^\circ$.
For $d>0$,
\[
 [\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y}]=\varepsilon[{\omega_y}],\qquad
 \int_{X_y}\operatorname{tr}_{{\omega_y}}(\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y}){\omega_y}^d
 =d\varepsilon V_F.
\]
On $f^{-1}(K')$, $\Omega, {\omega}^d\wedge f^*\chi_Y^m$ are equivalent;
hence fiber integration yields
\[
 \int_{f^{-1}(K)}\operatorname{tr}_{{\omega_y}}(\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y})\Omega
 \leq C_K\varepsilon.
\]
The dual norm decreases on restriction, so
\begin{align*}
 |\nabla_Vu_\varepsilon|_{{\omega_y}}^2
 &\leq|\nabla h_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2
              \operatorname{tr}_{{\omega_y}}(\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y}),\\
 \int_{f^{-1}(K)}|\nabla_Vu_\varepsilon|_{{\omega_y}}\Omega
 &\leq C_K\left(\int_X|\nabla u_\varepsilon|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2d\mu_\varepsilon\right)^{1/2}
              \varepsilon^{1/2}\leq C_K\sqrt\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
The smooth compact family of connected fibers has a uniform
$L^1$ Poincar\'e inequality:
\[
 \int_{X_y}|u_\varepsilon-\bar u_\varepsilon(y)|{\omega_y}^d
 \leq C_K\int_{X_y}|\nabla_V u_\varepsilon|_{{\omega_y}}{\omega_y}^d.
\]
Integrating proves the second estimate. Passing to distributions,
$\nabla_V u=0$; connectedness gives fiberwise constancy.

\quad\text{ in every }L^p(X,\Omega)\quad (p<\infty).

\end{enumerate}

label: lem:am-limit
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a smooth $\varphi\in \operatorname{PSH}(Y,\chi_Y)$, one has \[
    E_{\varepsilon}(f^*\varphi)=\frac{1}{V_{\varepsilon}}\int_X\int_0^1f^*\varphi(\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+tdd^c f^*\varphi)^ndt
    \]
    Since powers of a pull-back form above degree $m$ vanish, uniformly for $t\in [0,1]$, \[
\begin{aligned}
        &\int_X f^*\varphi\,
       \bigl(\chi+tdd^c f^*\varphi+\varepsilon{\omega}\bigr)^n\\
 &\quad=\sum_{k=d}^n\binom nk\varepsilon^k
       \int_X f^*\bigl(\varphi(\chi_Y+tdd^c\varphi)^{n-k}\bigr)
                      \wedge{\omega}^k\\
 &\quad=\binom nd\varepsilon^dV_F
       \int_Y\varphi(\chi_Y+tdd^c\varphi)^m+O_\varphi(\varepsilon^{d+1}),\\
 &V_\varepsilon=\binom nd\varepsilon^dV_FV_Y+O(\varepsilon^{d+1}).
    \end{aligned}
    \]
Here we used that $f_*({\omega}^d)=V_F$, so division cancels the factor
$\binom nd\varepsilon^dV_F$:\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_\varepsilon(f^*\varphi)
 &=\frac1{V_Y}\int_0^1\int_Y
       \varphi\bigl((1-t)\chi_Y+t\chi_\varphi\bigr)^m\,dt+O_\varphi(\varepsilon)\\
 &=\frac1{(m+1)V_Y}\sum_{j=0}^m
       \int_Y\varphi\chi_\varphi^j\wedge\chi_Y^{m-j}
          +O_\varphi(\varepsilon)
 =E_Y(\varphi)+O_\varphi(\varepsilon).
\end{aligned}
\]
A similar argument also shows that \[
\frac{(\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+dd^c f^*\varphi)^n}{V_\varepsilon}\to \frac{{\omega}^d\wedge f^*(\chi_Y+dd^c\varphi)^m}{V_F V_Y},
\]
and integration along fiber gives \[
f_*\left(\frac{{\omega}^d\wedge f^*(\chi_Y+dd^c\varphi)^m}{V_F V_Y}\right)=V_Y^{-1}(\chi_Y+dd^c\varphi)^m.
\]
Note that the energy $E_\varepsilon$ is concave, so \[
\begin{aligned}
&E_{\varepsilon}(\varphi_\varepsilon)\leq E_\varepsilon(f^*\varphi)+\int_X(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*\varphi)\frac{(\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+dd^c f^*\varphi)^n}{V_\varepsilon}\\
&E_{\varepsilon}(\varphi_\varepsilon)\geq E_\varepsilon(f^*\varphi)+\int_X(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*\varphi)d\mu_\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking $\varepsilon\to 0$, we have \[
\begin{aligned}
    &\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}E_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\leq E_Y(\varphi)+\int_Y(u-\varphi)\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi),\\
    &\liminf_{\varepsilon\to 0}E_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\geq E_Y(\varphi)+\int_Y(u-\varphi)d\nu.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here, we used \[
 \begin{aligned}
\left|\int_X(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u)\,d\mu_\varepsilon\right|
 &\leq C\|\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}\longrightarrow0,\\
 \left|\int_X f^*(u-\varphi)
        \bigl(e^{F_\varepsilon}-e^{f^*F}\bigr)\Omega\right|
 &\leq\|u-\varphi\|_\infty
       \|e^{F_\varepsilon}-e^{f^*F}\|_{L^1(\Omega)}\longrightarrow0,
 \end{aligned}
\]Since $\varphi_\varepsilon$ and $F_\varepsilon$ are uniformly bounded. 

Now we choose a sequence of bounded smooth $\varphi_j\in \operatorname{PSH}(\mathbb{CP}^N,\ell^{-1}\omega_{FS})$ that $\varphi_j\downarrow u$. First let $\varepsilon\to 0$ with $j$ fixed. Since $\varphi_j-u\geq 0$, we have \[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_Y(\varphi_j)+\int_Y(u-\varphi_j)\,d\nu
 &\leq\liminf_{\varepsilon\to0}E_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\\
 &\leq\limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}E_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\\
 &\leq E_Y(\varphi_j)+\int_Y(u-\varphi_j)\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi_j)
 \leq E_Y(\varphi_j).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let $j\to \infty$, \[
E_Y(\varphi_j)\downarrow E_Y(u),\qquad \int_Y(u-\varphi_j)d\nu\to 0.
\]
Hence $E_{\varepsilon}(\varphi_\varepsilon)\to E_Y(u)$. Moreover, we have \[
E_Y(u)\geq E_Y(\varphi)+\int_Y(u-\varphi)d\nu
\]
for any smooth  $\varphi\in \operatorname{PSH}(Y,\chi_Y)$. Apply the decreasing approximation again, it follows that the above inequality holds for any bounded $\varphi\in \operatorname{PSH}(Y,\chi_Y)$. The equation follows from the variational formula discussed before.

label: eq:c-8
title: Proof
body_md:
If $n=1$, then $m=1$, $d=0$, and $f$ is an isomorphism of smooth
curves. Both conclusions follow from $V_\varepsilon\to V_Y$.
For the rest of the proof assume $n\geq2$.
Fix smooth $\varphi$ with $\chi_Y+dd^c \varphi\ge\delta\chi_Y$, put $\widehat\omega=\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+dd^c f^*\varphi$, $h=\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*\varphi$, and 
\[
I_\varepsilon=V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int_Xh(\widehat\omega^n-\omega_\varepsilon^n)
=V_\varepsilon^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\int_Xi\partial h\wedge\bar\partial h\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^k\wedge\widehat\omega^{n-1-k}.
\]
We claim that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-8}
I_\varepsilon\to I_Y(u,\varphi):=\int_Y(u-\varphi)(\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi)-\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)).
\end{equation}
Recall the binomial expansion in Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit}:\[
\frac{\widehat{\omega}^n}{V_\varepsilon}=\frac{{\omega}^d\wedge f^*(\chi_Y+dd^c \varphi)^m}{V_FV_Y}+O_{\varphi}(\varepsilon)\Omega\leq C_{\varphi}\Omega.
\]
Write $h=(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u)+(f^*u-\varphi)$. Then 
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_Xh\,\widehat\omega^n
                   -\int_Y(u-\varphi)\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi)\right|\\
 &\quad\leq
 \left|\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_X
             (\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u)\widehat\omega^n\right|
 +\left|\int_X f^*(u-\varphi)
       \left(\frac{\widehat\omega^n}{V_\varepsilon}
             -\frac{{\omega}^d\wedge f^*\chi_\varphi^m}{V_FV_Y}\right)\right|\\
 &\quad\leq C_\varphi\|\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}
       +C_\varphi\varepsilon\|u-\varphi\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For the second integral, Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit} has already proved
$\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)=e^Ff_*\Omega$. Thus
\[
 \begin{aligned}
&\left|\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_Xh\,\omega_\varepsilon^n
-\int_Y(u-\varphi)\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)\right|\\
 &\quad\leq
 \left|\int_X(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u)e^{F_\varepsilon}\Omega\right|+\left|\int_Xf^*(u-\varphi)(e^{F_\varepsilon}-e^{f^*F})\Omega\right|\\
 &\quad\leq C\|\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+\|u-\varphi\|_{L^\infty}\|e^{F_\varepsilon}-e^{f^*F}\|_{L^1(\Omega)}
       \longrightarrow0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last limit uses $e^{F_\varepsilon}\leq C$ and
$\|e^{F_\varepsilon}-e^{f^*F}\|_{L^1}
\leq C\|F_\varepsilon-f^*F\|_{L^1}\to0$.
Subtracting these two limits proves the claim. 

Next, for smooth compactly supported $(1,1)$ test form $\Xi$ on $Y^\circ$, pair it with $f_*(V_\varepsilon^{-1}(\widehat{\omega}^{n-1}-\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}))$. The pairing is a sum of the following terms
\[
V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int_Xi\partial h\wedge\bar\partial f^*\Xi\wedge T_k,
\qquad T_k=\omega_\varepsilon^k\wedge\widehat\omega^{n-2-k}.
\]
All covectors of $\bar\partial f^*\Xi$ are horizontal with bounded coefficients in $\chi$.  Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-9}
\left|V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int i\partial h\wedge\bar\partial f^*\Xi\wedge T_k\right|
\le C_\Xi
\left(V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int i\partial h\wedge\bar\partial h\wedge\chi\wedge T_k\right)^{1/2}
\left(V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int\chi^2\wedge T_k\right)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
Since $\widehat\omega\ge\delta\chi$, the first squared factor is at most $\delta^{-1}I_\varepsilon$. The other squared factor is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_\varepsilon^{-1}\int_X\chi^2\wedge T_k
 &=\frac{[\chi]^2[\chi_\varepsilon]^{n-2}}{V_\varepsilon}\\
 &=\frac{\binom{n-2}{d}\varepsilon^dV_FV_Y+O(\varepsilon^{d+1})}
         {\binom nd\varepsilon^dV_FV_Y+O(\varepsilon^{d+1})}
 \longrightarrow\frac{m(m-1)}{n(n-1)}\qquad(m\geq2).
 \end{aligned}
\]
 If $m=1$, this factor is identically
zero because $\chi^2=0$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-10}
\left|\left\langle\Xi,f_*\frac{\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}-\widehat\omega_{\varepsilon,\varphi}^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}\right\rangle\right|
\le C_\Xi\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt{I_\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}

For $0<\delta<1$, put $v_\delta=(1-\delta)u$, so that
$\chi_{v_\delta}=(1-\delta)\chi_u+\delta\chi_Y\geq\delta\chi_Y$.
For bounded psh functions, we have 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-11}
 \begin{split}
 I_Y(u,v_\delta)
 &=\frac{\delta^2}{V_Y}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}
    \int_Yi\partial u\wedge\bar\partial u
              \wedge\chi_u^k\wedge\chi_{v_\delta}^{m-1-k}\\
 &\leq2m\|u\|_{L^\infty}\delta^2.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $T=\chi_u^k\wedge\chi_{v_\delta}^{m-1-k}$, bounded
Bedford--Taylor integration by parts on the resolution yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\leq\int_Yi\partial u\wedge\bar\partial u\wedge T
 &=-\int_Yu\,dd^cu\wedge T
   =\int_Yu(\chi_Y-\chi_u)\wedge T\\
 &\leq\|u\|_\infty\int_Y(\chi_Y+\chi_u)\wedge T
   =2\|u\|_{L^\infty} V_Y.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the uniform bound in \eqref{eq:c-11}.

Choose smooth $u_j\downarrow u$, and set
$\varphi_{\delta,j}=(1-\delta)u_j$.
The three limits are taken in the order
$\varepsilon\to0$, then $j\to\infty$, then $\delta\to0$.
For fixed $\delta,j$, direct computation gives
\[
 f_*\left(\frac{(\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+dd^c f^*\varphi_{j,\delta})^{n-1}}
                         {V_\varepsilon}\right)
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\binom{n-1}{d}V_F}{\binom nd V_FV_Y}
                 ( \chi_Y+dd^c \varphi_{\delta,j})^{m-1}
 =\frac{m}{nV_Y}(\chi_Y+dd^c \varphi_{\delta,j})^{m-1}.
\]
Hence \eqref{eq:c-8} and \eqref{eq:c-10} imply
\[
 \limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}
 \left|\left\langle\Xi,\,
 f_*\frac{\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}
       -\frac{m}{nV_Y}\chi_{\varphi_{\delta,j}}^{m-1}
 \right\rangle\right|
 \leq C_\Xi\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt{I_Y(u,\varphi_{\delta,j})}.
\]
For fixed $\delta$, monotone convergence of the Bedford-Taylor products implies 
\[
I_Y(u,\varphi_{\delta,j})\longrightarrow I_Y(u,v_\delta),\qquad
 (\chi_Y+dd^c{\varphi_{\delta,j}})^{m-1}\rightharpoonup(\chi_Y+dd^c{v_\delta})^{m-1}.
\]
Letting $j\to\infty$ in the preceding estimate and using
\eqref{eq:c-11}, we obtain
\[
 \limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}
 \left|\left\langle\Xi,\,
 f_*\frac{\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}
       -\frac{m}{nV_Y}(\chi_Y+dd^c{v_\delta})^{m-1}
 \right\rangle\right|
 \leq C_\Xi\sqrt\delta.
\]
Finally,
\[
 (\chi_Y+dd^c{v_\delta})^{m-1}
 =\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\binom{m-1}{k}
      (1-\delta)^k\delta^{m-1-k}
                     (\chi_Y+dd^c u)^k\wedge\chi_Y^{m-1-k}
 \rightharpoonup(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}.
\]
Let $\delta\to0$ to obtain \eqref{eq:c-6}. These formulas also
hold when $m=1$.

\emph{Proof of \textup{(2)}.}
The bounds for $F_\varepsilon$ and
$\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi$ imply
\[
0\leq\frac{\chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}
 =\frac1n(\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi)e^{F_\varepsilon}\Omega
 \leq C\Omega.
\]
Thus, for every bounded nonnegative measurable $b$ on $Y$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\leq\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_Xf^*b\,
                       \chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}
 &\leq C\int_X f^*b\,\Omega=C\int_Y b\,f_*\Omega.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently, as positive measures on $Y$,
\[
 0\leq
 f_*\!\left(\frac{\chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}\right)
 \leq C f_*\Omega .
\]

For $b\in C^\infty_c(Y^\circ)$, apply \textup{(i)} with the
test form $\Xi=b\chi_Y$. Since $\chi=f^*\chi_Y$, this gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_X f^*b\,
                          \chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}
 &=\left\langle b\chi_Y,\,
                 f_*\frac{\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}}{V_\varepsilon}
   \right\rangle\\
 &\longrightarrow
 \frac{m}{nV_Y}\int_{Y^\circ}b\,\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For nonnegative $b$, the preceding bound passes to this limit.
Consequently,
\[
 0\leq\frac{m}{nV_Y}\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}
 \leq C f_*\Omega\quad\text{on }Y^\circ.
\]
Recall $D=Y\setminus Y^\circ$. Its inverse image is proper analytic,
and bounded Bedford--Taylor products give no mass to proper
analytic sets on a resolution.
Therefore
\[
 (f_*\Omega)(D)=\int_{f^{-1}(D)}\Omega=0,\qquad
 \int_D\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}=0.
\]
The same measure inequality thus holds on all of $Y$.

It remains to allow test functions without compact support in
$Y^\circ$. Fix $b\in L^1(Y,f_*\Omega)$. The restriction of
$f_*\Omega$ to $Y^\circ$ is a smooth positive volume form; it has
finite total mass and gives no mass to $D$. Smooth approximation
and exhaustion of $Y^\circ$ therefore give
\[
 b_j\in C^\infty_c(Y^\circ),\qquad
 \|b_j-b\|_{L^1(f_*\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The two measure bounds imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_X f^*(b-b_j)\,
                          \chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}\right|
 \leq C\|b-b_j\|_{L^1(f_*\Omega)},\\
 &\left|\frac{m}{nV_Y}\int_Y(b-b_j)\,
                          \chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}\right|
 \leq C\|b-b_j\|_{L^1(f_*\Omega)}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
First let $\varepsilon\to0$ with $j$ fixed, using the convergence
already proved for $b_j$. The triangle inequality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}
 \left|\frac1{V_\varepsilon}\int_Xf^*b\,
                          \chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}
       -\frac{m}{nV_Y}\int_Yb\,\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}\right|\\
 &\qquad\leq2C\|b-b_j\|_{L^1(f_*\Omega)}
       \xrightarrow{j\to\infty}0 .
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:c-7}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Direct computation shows \[
    \frac{d}{dt}|_{t=0}J_{\chi,\varepsilon}(\varphi+th)=V_{\varepsilon}^{-1}\int_Xh\chi\wedge(\chi+\varepsilon{\omega}+dd^c\varphi)^{n-1},
    \]
   and \[
   \frac{d}{dt}|_{t=0}J_{\chi_Y,Y}(\varphi+th)=V_Y\int_Yh\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c\varphi)^{m-1}.
   \]
Moreover \[
\frac{d^2}{dt^2}|_{t=0}J_{\chi,\varepsilon}\leq 0, \qquad \frac{d^2}{dt^2}|_{t=0}J_{\chi_Y,Y}\leq 0.\]
Then similar expansion in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit} gives, for fixed smooth psh function $\varphi\in \operatorname{PSH}(Y,\chi_Y)$, \[
J_{\chi,\varepsilon}(f^*\varphi)\to \frac{m}{n}J_{\chi_Y,Y}(\varphi).
\]
Note that $|F_\varepsilon|, \operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi$ are uniformly bounded,\[
\left|\frac{1}{V_\varepsilon}\int_X(\varphi_\varepsilon-f^*u)\chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}\right|\leq C\|\varphi_{\varepsilon}-f^*u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\|\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\|_{L^2(\mu_\varepsilon)}\to 0.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:mix-current}, \[
\frac{1}{V_\varepsilon}\int_Xf^*(u-\varphi)\chi\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^{n-1}\to \frac{m}{nV_Y}\int_Y(u-\varphi)\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}. 
\]
Hence, a similar concavity argument as in Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit} gives, \[
\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}nJ_{\chi,\varepsilon}(\varphi_\varepsilon)\leq mJ_{\chi_Y,Y}(\varphi)+\frac{m}{V_Y}\int_Y(u-\varphi)\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c\varphi)^{m-1},
\]
\[
\liminf_{\varepsilon\to 0}nJ_{\chi,\varepsilon}(\varphi_\varepsilon)\geq mJ_{\chi_Y,Y}(\varphi)+\frac{m}{V_Y}\int_Y(u-\varphi)\chi_Y\wedge(\chi_Y+dd^c u)^{m-1}.
\]

We choose $\varphi_j\downarrow u$, with $\varphi_j\in \operatorname{PSH}(\mathbb C P^N,\ell^{-1}\omega_{FS})$ being smooth. Monotone convergence of the mixed energies gives the desired convergence.

body_md:
\label{lem:canonical-volume-density}

label: eq:mabuchi-energy
title: Proof
body_md:
For a smooth $\chi_\varepsilon$-psh function $\varphi$, the normalized Mabuchi energy is defined as \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:mabuchi-energy}
        \mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\varphi):=\frac{1}{V_\varepsilon}\int_X\log{\frac{(\chi_\varepsilon+dd^c\varphi)^n}{V_\varepsilon\Omega}}(\chi_\varepsilon+dd^c\varphi)^n+nJ_{\chi,\varepsilon}(\varphi)+\underline{R}_\varepsilon E_{\varepsilon}(\varphi)
    \end{equation}
The Mabuchi energy is convex along geodesics, and cscK metrics minimize it.
Now we apply this to two family of metrics:\begin{enumerate}
    \item For ${\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon$, the potential $\psi_\varepsilon\to f^*\varphi_{\rm can}$, and $\nu_{\rm can}=e^{f^*\varphi_{\rm can}}f_*\Omega$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon}\chi\leq C$.
    \item For $\omega_\varepsilon$, by passing to subsequence, the potential $\varphi_\varepsilon\to f^*u$, and $\nu_u=e^Ff_*\Omega=\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\leq C$.
\end{enumerate}
On $Y$, one has \[
mJ_{\chi_Y,Y}(u)=(m+1)E_Y(u)-\int_Yu\operatorname{MA}_Y(u).
\]
Since $\underline{R}_\varepsilon\to -m$ and the bounded $\log$-density converges in $L^1$, we get \[
\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\to \int_YFe^{f^*F}f_*\Omega+mJ_{\chi_Y,Y}(u)-mE_Y(u)=\int_YFe^{f^*F}f_*\Omega+E_Y(u)-\int_Yu\operatorname{MA}_Y(u).
\]
The same argument in Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit},\ref{lem:mix-current},\ref{lem:mixed-energy} also works for ${\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon$, and we get \[
\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\psi_\varepsilon)\to \int_Y\varphi_{\rm can}e^{\varphi_{\rm can}}f_*\Omega+E_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})-\int_Y\varphi_{\rm can}\operatorname{MA}_{Y}(\varphi_{\rm can}).
\]
Since $\omega_\varepsilon$ is the unique cscK metric, we have $\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\varphi_\varepsilon)\leq \mathcal{M}_{\varepsilon}(\psi_\varepsilon)$.


Note that from concavity, we also have \[
E_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})\leq E_Y(u)+\int_Y(\varphi_{\rm can}-u)\operatorname{MA}_Y(u).
\]

Therefore \[
\begin{aligned}
    0\geq& \int_Y(Fe^{f^*F}-\varphi_{\rm can}e^{\varphi_{\rm can}})f_*\Omega+E_Y(u)-E_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})-\int_Yu\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)+\int_Y\varphi_{\rm can}\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})\\
    =&\int_X(F-\varphi_{\rm can}) e^Ff_*\Omega+E_Y(u)-E_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})-\int_Y(u-\varphi_{\rm can})\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)\\
    \ge &\int_Y(F-\varphi_{\rm can})e^Ff_*\Omega.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here we used that $\operatorname{MA}_Y(u)=e^Ff_*\Omega$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:am-limit}, and the equation of the canonical metric on the base $\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})=e^{\varphi_{\rm can}}f_*\Omega$. 

Now the difference of the entropy term \[
\int_Y(F-\varphi_{\rm can})e^Ff_*\Omega=\int_Y(F-\varphi_{\rm can})e^{F-\varphi_{\rm can}}\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})=\int_Y(s\log s-s+1)\operatorname{MA}_Y(\varphi_{\rm can})\geq 0,
\]where we let $s=e^{F-\varphi_{\rm can}}$ and used the facts that $s\log s-s+1\geq 0$ and $=$ attains only at $s=1$. Therefore, every inequality is equality. In particular, $s=1$ almost everywhere, i.e. \[
F=\varphi_{\rm can}.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:entropy-to-metric
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:entropy-to-metric}
Let $\omega,\widehat\omega$ be cohomologous K\"ahler forms on a compact
complex $n$-fold. Set
$V=\int_X\omega^n$, $\mu=\omega^n/V$, and $\nu=\widehat\omega^n/V$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{item:entropy-bound}
\[
 \int_X|\widehat\omega-\omega|_\omega\,d\mu
 \leq2\sqrt{n\operatorname{Ent}_\nu(\mu)},\qquad
 \text{ where }\operatorname{Ent}_\nu(\mu)=\int_X\log\frac{d\mu}{d\nu}d\mu.
\]
\item\label{item:entropy-convergence}
Suppose $\mu_j=\rho_j\Omega$, $\nu_j=\widehat\rho_j\Omega$, where
$C^{-1}\leq\rho_j,\widehat\rho_j\leq C$ and
$\|\rho_j-\widehat\rho_j\|_{L^1(\Omega)}\to0$. Then
\[
 \int_X|\widehat\omega_j-\omega_j|_{\omega_j}\,d\mu_j\to0,
 \qquad
 \int_X|\omega_j-\widehat\omega_j|_{\widehat\omega_j}\,d\nu_j\to0.
\]
For every $\eta>0$, outside a set of $\Omega$-measure tending to zero,
\[
 (1-\eta)\omega_j\leq\widehat\omega_j\leq(1+\eta)\omega_j.
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note the following elementary inequality 
\[
 (\sqrt t-1)^2\leq t-1-\log t,\qquad
 (\sqrt t+1)^2\leq2(t+1),\qquad
 |t-1|=|\sqrt t-1|(\sqrt t+1).
\]
It follows that 
\[
 |\widehat\omega-\omega|_\omega^2
 \leq2(\operatorname{tr}_\omega\widehat\omega+n)
 \left(\operatorname{tr}_\omega\widehat\omega-n-
                    \log\frac{\widehat\omega^n}{\omega^n}\right).
\]
The first factor is bounded due to the cohomology class
\[
\int_X\operatorname{tr}_\omega\widehat\omega d\mu
 =\frac{n}{V}\int_X\widehat\omega\wedge\omega^{n-1}=n,
\]
and 
\[
 \int_X\left(\operatorname{tr}_\omega\widehat\omega-n-
                 \log\frac{\widehat\omega^n}{\omega^n}\right)d\mu
 =\operatorname{Ent}_\nu(\mu).
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, one gets (i).

For (2),
\[
 0\leq\operatorname{Ent}_{\nu_j}(\mu_j)
 \leq C^2\|\rho_j-\widehat\rho_j\|_{L^1(\Omega)}\to0,
\]
and likewise with the measures interchanged. Finally,
\[
 |\widehat\omega_j-\omega_j|_{\omega_j}\leq\eta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 -\eta\omega_j\leq\widehat\omega_j-\omega_j\leq\eta\omega_j;
\]
Markov's inequality gives the last assertion.
head: environment

label: cor:Lp-convergence-in-base-direction
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Lp-convergence-in-base-direction}
 For every smooth $(1,0)$-form $\alpha$ on $Y^\circ$, and $K\Subset Y^\circ$
\[|f^*\alpha|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2
 \longrightarrow f^*|\alpha|_{\omega_{\rm can}}^2
 \quad\text{in }L^p(f^{-1}(K),\Omega),\quad p<\infty.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:entropy-to-metric} to $\omega_\varepsilon$ and
${\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon$. Their normalized densities are uniformly
bounded above and below and have the same total-variation limit.
The uniform convergence of the metric in regular part in Theorem~\ref{thm:NKRF-convergence} gives
\[
 (1-o_K(1))(f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon\omega_{\rm SRF})\leq{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon
 \leq(1+o_K(1))(f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon\omega_{\rm SRF}).
\]
Use the $\omega_{\rm SRF}$-orthogonal complement of the vertical
tangent bundle. The reference form has zero mixed term; its
horizontal restriction is $f^*\omega_{\rm can}+O_K(\varepsilon)$
and its vertical restriction is $\varepsilon\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}$.
Since $f^*\alpha$ vanishes on vertical vectors, duality gives
\[|f^*\alpha|_{{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon}^2\longrightarrow f^*|\alpha|_{\omega_{\rm can}}^2\quad\hbox{uniformly on }f^{-1}(K).
\]
When $d=0$, this follows directly from convergence of positive
metrics on $f^{-1}(K)$.
For $0<\eta<1$, outside a set of measure tending to zero,
\[
 (1-\eta)\omega_\varepsilon\leq{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon\leq(1+\eta)\omega_\varepsilon,
\]
so duality gives
\[
 (1-\eta)|f^*\alpha|_{{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon}^2\leq|f^*\alpha|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\leq(1+\eta)|f^*\alpha|_{{\tilde\omega}_\varepsilon}^2.
\]
The comparison-family limit gives convergence in measure as
$\eta\downarrow0$. Since
$|f^*\alpha|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2
\leq C_\alpha\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\leq C_\alpha$,
the convergence holds in every finite $L^p$.

label: lem:iteration
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:dg4
title: Proof
body_md:
Suppress $\varepsilon$ and use
$\mu_\varepsilon$ for all integrals and norms.
We first estimate $U_+=\max\{U,0\}$. For $\delta>0$, set
\[
 v=U_++\|\Delta_\omega U\|_{L^{p_*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}))}+\delta,
 \qquad
 \left\|\frac{|\Delta_\omega U|}{v}\right\|_{L^{p_*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}))}
 \leq1.
\]
$-\Delta_\omega U_+\leq|\Delta_\omega U|$ in the weak sense, 
hence $-\Delta_\omega v\leq|\Delta_\omega U|$.
For $p\geq2$ and $\xi=\xi_{s,t}$, use the nonnegative test function
$\xi^2v^{p-1}$.
All integrals in the next display are over
$f^{-1}(B_t)$, and all differential norms use $\omega_\varepsilon$.
Integration by parts and Young's inequality give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (p-1)\int\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2
 &\leq2\int\xi v^{p-1}|\nabla\xi|\,|\nabla v|
       +\int\frac{|\Delta_\omega U|}{v}\,\xi^2v^p\\
 &\leq\frac{p-1}{2}\int\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2
       +\frac{2}{p-1}\int v^p|\nabla\xi|^2
       +\int\frac{|\Delta_\omega U|}{v}\,\xi^2v^p.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The cutoff bound and the uniform Sobolev inequality imply
\[
 \|\xi v^{p/2}\|_{L^{2q}}^2
 \leq Cp^2\left[
       \bigl(1+(t-s)^{-2}\bigr)\int_{f^{-1}(B_t)}v^p+\int_{f^{-1}(B_t)}\frac{|\Delta_\omega U|}{v}(\xi v^{p/2})^2\right].
\]
Put $p_*'=p_*/(p_*-1)<q$ and
$\theta=q/[p_*(q-1)]\in(0,1)$. For $h=\xi v^{p/2}$,
H\"older's inequality and interpolation give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
\int\frac{|\Delta_\omega U|}{v}h^2&\leq\|h\|_{L^{2p_*'}}^2
\leq\|h\|_{L^{2q}}^{2\theta}\|h\|_{L^2}^{2(1-\theta)}\\
&\leq\tau\|h\|_{L^{2q}}^2+C_\theta\tau^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}\|h\|_{L^2}^2\qquad(\tau>0).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Choose $\tau=(2Cp^2)^{-1}$ and absorb the first term. Since
$\|h\|_{L^2}^2\leq\int_{f^{-1}(B_t)}v^p$ and $\xi=1$ on $f^{-1}(B_s)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dg4}
 \|v\|_{L^{pq}(f^{-1}(B_s))}
 \leq\left[Cp^{2/(1-\theta)}\bigl(1+(t-s)^{-2}\bigr)\right]^{1/p}\|v\|_{L^p(f^{-1}(B_t))}.
\end{equation}

Set $r_l=r(1+2^{-l})$ and $p_l=2q^l$. Taking
$(s,t,p)=(r_{l+1},r_l,p_l)$ in \eqref{eq:dg4} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:dg5}
 \|v\|_{L^{p_{l+1}}(f^{-1}(B_{r_{l+1}}))}
 \leq\left(C_r4^lp_l^{2/(1-\theta)}\right)^{1/p_l}\|v\|_{L^{p_l}(f^{-1}(B_{r_l}))}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[\prod_{l=0}^\infty\left(C_r4^lp_l^{2/(1-\theta)}\right)^{1/p_l}<\infty,
\qquad\|v\|_{L^\infty(f^{-1}(B_r))}
\leq C\|v\|_{L^2(f^{-1}(B_{2r}))}.
\]
Since $U_+\leq v$ and $\mu_\varepsilon(X)=1$,
\[
 \|U_+\|_{L^\infty(f^{-1}(B_r))}
 \leq C\left(\|U_+\|_{L^2(f^{-1}(B_{2r}))}
       +\|\Delta_\omega U\|_{L^{p_*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}))}+\delta\right).
\]
Let $\delta\downarrow0$. The same argument for $-U$ estimates
$U_-=(-U)_+$ and proves the desired estimate.

label: lem:Linfty-density
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Linfty-density}
     For any compact $K\Subset X^\circ$, $\|F_\varepsilon-f^*\varphi_{\rm can}\|_{L^\infty(K)}\to 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $q/(q-1)<p_*<\infty$. On any coordinate ball $B_{2r}\Subset Y^\circ$, set $U=F_\varepsilon-f^*\varphi$. Then one has \[
    \Delta_{\omega_\varepsilon}U=-\underline{R}_\varepsilon-\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi-\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_{\varepsilon}}(f^*(\omega_{\rm can}-\chi_Y))=-\underline{R}_\varepsilon-\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}f^*\omega_{\rm can}.
    \]
    Choose a smooth $\omega_{\rm can}$-unitary $(1,0)$-froms $\alpha_1,...,\alpha_m$ on a neighborhood of $B_{2r}$. Then by Lemma~\ref{cor:Lp-convergence-in-base-direction}, and $|F_\varepsilon|\leq C$, \[
    \omega_{\rm can}=\sqrt{-1}\sum_i\alpha_j\wedge\bar{\alpha}_j, \quad \operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}f^*\omega_{\rm can}\to m \text{ in } L^{p^*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)
    \]
Combined with $\underline{R}_\varepsilon\to -m$, it follows that \[
\|\Delta_{\omega_\varepsilon}U\|_{L^{p^*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)}\leq |\underline{R}_{\varepsilon}+m|+\|\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}f^*\omega_{\rm can}-m\|_{L^{p^*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)}\to 0.
\]
Moreover, we showed in Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-volume-density} that $F_\varepsilon\to f^*\varphi\
_{\rm can}$ in $L^p$ for any finite $p$. Hence $\|U\|_{L^{p^*}(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)}\to 0$. For any given $K\Subset X^\circ$, choose finitely many coordinate balls such that \[
f(K)\subset \cup_{j=1}^MB_{r_{j}}, \quad B_{2r_j}\Subset Y^\circ.
\]
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:iteration}, we get the desired $L^\infty$ convergence.
head: environment

label: lem:sharp-schwarz-estimate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sharp-schwarz-estimate}
    For every $K\Subset X^\circ$, $\omega_\varepsilon\geq (1-o(1))f^*\omega_{\rm can}$
head: environment

label: eq:sharp-schwarz-bochner
title: Proof
body_md:
Work over $B_{2r}\Subset Y^\circ$, with base coordinates
$y^1,\ldots,y^m$. For
$a=\sum_{\alpha=1}^m a_\alpha\,dy^\alpha$ with constant coefficients
and $|a|_{\omega_{\rm can}}\leq1$ on $B_{2r}$, set
\[\omega_a=\sqrt{-1}a\wedge\bar a,\qquad u_\varepsilon=\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}f^*\omega_a,\qquad
u_0=\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_{\rm can}}\omega_a.
\]
We have
\[
 0\leq u_\varepsilon\leq C,\qquad
 \|u_\varepsilon-f^*u_0\|_{L^2(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Suppress $\varepsilon$ and put
\[
 h=\sum_{\alpha=1}^m a_\alpha(y^\alpha\circ f),\qquad
 f^*a=\partial h,\qquad
f^*\omega_a=\sqrt{-1}\,\partial h\wedge\bar\partial\bar h.
\]
Fix $x\in f^{-1}(B_{2r})$ and choose holomorphic coordinates
$z^1,\ldots,z^n$ normal for $\omega$ at $x$:
\[
 \omega=\sqrt{-1}g_{i\bar j}\,dz^i\wedge d\bar z^j,\qquad
 g_{i\bar j}(x)=\delta_{ij},\qquad
 \partial_k g_{i\bar j}(x)=0.
\]
Write $h_i=\partial_i h$, $h_{ik}=\partial_k\partial_i h$, with
$\sum_jg^{i\bar j}g_{k\bar j}=\delta^i_k$. Since $h$ is holomorphic,
\[
 u=\sum_{i,j}g^{i\bar j}h_i\overline{h_j},\qquad
 \partial_{\bar l}h_i=0,\qquad
 \partial_k\overline{h_j}=0.
\]
Straightforward computation gives  
\[
 \partial_k u
 =\sum_{i,j}(\partial_k g^{i\bar j})h_i\overline{h_j}
  +\sum_{i,j}g^{i\bar j}h_{ik}\overline{h_j}.
\]
\[
 u_{k\bar l}=\sum_{i,j}(\partial_k\partial_{\bar l}g^{i\bar j})h_i\overline{h_j}+\sum_ih_{ik}\overline{h_{il}}.
\]
At 
$x$, we have
\[
 \begin{aligned}
\partial_k\partial_{\bar l}g^{i\bar j}
 &=-\partial_k\partial_{\bar l}g_{j\bar i}
   =R_{j\bar i k\bar l}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, using $\operatorname{Ric}(\omega)=-\chi-dd^c F$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta_\omega u
 &=\sum_{i,k}|h_{ik}|^2+\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Ric}(\omega)_{j\bar i}h_i\overline{h_j}\\
 &=\sum_{i,k}|h_{ik}|^2
   -\sum_{i,j}\chi_{j\bar i}h_i\overline{h_j}-\sum_{i,j}F_{j\bar i}h_i\overline{h_j}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-schwarz-bochner}
 \begin{split}
 \Delta_\omega u
 &=|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|_\omega^2
   -\langle f^*\omega_a,\chi\rangle_\omega\\
 &\qquad-\langle f^*\omega_a,dd^c F\rangle_\omega.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
It is also \eqref{eq:map-bochner-coordinates} for the holomorphic
map $h$ to flat $\mathbb C$. A unitary change of the normal coordinates
diagonalizes $\chi$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i\geq0$, so
\[
 0\leq\langle f^*\omega_a,\chi\rangle_\omega=\sum_i\lambda_i|h_i|^2\leq\left(\sum_i\lambda_i\right)\left(\sum_i|h_i|^2\right)
 =(\operatorname{tr}_\omega\chi)u\leq Cu.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \Delta_\omega u\geq-Cu-\langle f^*\omega_a,dd^c F\rangle_\omega.
\]
We retain the square in \eqref{eq:sharp-schwarz-bochner} below.
The smoothness of $u_0$ on the fixed chart gives
\[
 |\nabla f^*u_0|_\omega^2\leq C\operatorname{tr}_\omega\chi\leq C,
 \qquad
 |\Delta_\omega f^*u_0|
 =|\operatorname{tr}_\omega f^*(dd^c u_0)|\leq C\operatorname{tr}_\omega\chi\leq C.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-schwarz-excess}
 \Delta_\omega(u-f^*u_0)\geq|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|_\omega^2-C-\langle f^*\omega_a,dd^c F\rangle_\omega.
\end{equation}

Set $v=(u-f^*u_0)_+$, $\xi=\xi_{s,t}$ and
$\psi=\xi^2v^{p-1}$, where $p\geq3$.
All following integrals use $d\mu_\varepsilon$ on $f^{-1}(B_t)$,
and all differential norms use $\omega$. Testing
\eqref{eq:sharp-schwarz-excess} with $\psi$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &(p-1)\int\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2+\int\psi|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|^2\\
 &\quad\leq2\int\xi v^{p-1}|\nabla\xi|\,|\nabla v| +C\int\psi+\int\psi\langle f^*\omega_a,dd^c F\rangle_\omega.
 \end{aligned}
\]
To estimate the last term, note that at the normal point
\[\nabla_k(f^*\omega_a)_{i\bar j}=h_{ik}\overline{h_j},\qquad
 \nabla_{\bar k}(f^*\omega_a)_{i\bar j}=h_i\overline{h_{jk}}.
\]
Hence
\[
|\nabla(f^*\omega_a)|_\omega\leq Cu^{1/2}|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|_\omega.
\]
Integration by parts,  and the bounds
$u+|\nabla F|_\omega\leq C$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:gradient} and
the trace estimate in base  give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
\left|\int\psi\langle f^*\omega_a,dd^c F\rangle_\omega\right|
 &\leq C\int\bigl(u|\nabla\psi|+\psi|\nabla(f^*\omega_a)|\bigr)|\nabla F|\\
&\leq\frac12\int\psi|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|^2+C\int(|\nabla\psi|+\psi).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the square is absorbed using
\[
C\psi|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|\leq\frac12\psi|\nabla^{1,0}_\omega(f^*a)|^2+C\psi.
\]
Since
\[
|\nabla\psi|\leq2\xi v^{p-1}|\nabla\xi|+(p-1)\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|,
\]
the remaining terms satisfy
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 2\xi v^{p-1}|\nabla\xi|\,|\nabla v|&\leq\frac{p-1}{4}\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2+\frac{C}{p-1}v^p|\nabla\xi|^2,\\
 C\xi v^{p-1}|\nabla\xi|&\leq Cv^p|\nabla\xi|^2+C\xi^2v^{p-2},\\
 C(p-1)\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|&\leq\frac{p-1}{4}\xi^2v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2+C(p-1)\xi^2v^{p-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
After absorption, the cutoff bound and $0\leq v\leq C$ imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-schwarz-energy}
\int|\nabla(\xi v^{p/2})|^2+\int\xi^2v^p
 \leq Cp^2\bigl(1+(t-s)^{-2}\bigr)\int_{f^{-1}(B_t)}v^{p-2}.
\end{equation}
The uniform Sobolev inequality therefore yields
\[
 \|v\|_{L^{pq}(f^{-1}(B_s))}^p
 \leq Cp^2\bigl(1+(t-s)^{-2}\bigr)\|v\|_{L^{p-2}(f^{-1}(B_t))}^{p-2}.
\]
Then Moser iteration implies
\[
\|v\|_{L^\infty(f^{-1}(B_r))}
 \leq C\|v\|_{L^2(f^{-1}(B_{2r}),\mu_\varepsilon)}^{(q-1)/(2q-1)}
\longrightarrow0.
\]

Write $u_\varepsilon(a),u_0(a)$ to denote the covector dependence. Since $\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\leq C$, for $|a|,|b|\leq1$,
\[
 |u_\varepsilon(a)-u_\varepsilon(b)|
 +f^*|u_0(a)-u_0(b)|\leq C|a-b|.
\]
For a finite $\delta$-net of the Euclidean unit covectors, the convergence of $v_+\to 0$ is uniform. Hence \[
\limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in f^{-1}(B_r)\\ |a|=1}}
       \bigl(u_\varepsilon(a)-f^*u_0(a)\bigr)
 \leq C\delta.
\]
Let $\delta\downarrow0$. Since $u_0(a)\geq c_r|a|^2$ on
$\overline{B_r}$, homogeneity gives
\[
|f^*\alpha|_{\omega_\varepsilon}^2\leq(1+o_r(1))f^*|\alpha|_{\omega_{\rm can}}^2
 \quad\text{on }f^{-1}(B_r),\qquad \alpha\in T^{*1,0}Y^\circ.
\]
For $Z\in T^{1,0}X$, duality then gives
\[
 |df(Z)|_{\omega_{\rm can}}
 =\sup_{|\alpha|_{\omega_{\rm can}}=1}|f^*\alpha(Z)|
 \leq(1+o_r(1))^{1/2}|Z|_{\omega_\varepsilon}.
\]
Finally choose
$K\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^N B_{r_j}$ with
$\overline{B_{2r_j}}\Subset Y^\circ$.
The maximum of the finitely many errors $o_{r_j}(1)$ tends to zero.
The preceding inequality is therefore equivalent to the desired sharp Schwarz-type estimate on
$f^{-1}(K)$.

title: Lemma
body_md: For any $K\Subset Y^\circ$, $\operatorname{osc}_{X_y}\varphi_\varepsilon\leq C_K\varepsilon$, for all $y\in K$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\chi|_{X_y}=0$, one has \[
    \varepsilon^{-1}\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y}={\omega_y}+dd^c_V v_{\varepsilon,y}, \quad h_{\varepsilon,y}:=\frac{(\varepsilon^{-1}\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y})^d}{{\omega_y}^d},
    \]
    where $v_{\varepsilon,y}:=\varepsilon^{-1}\left(\varphi_\varepsilon|_{X_y}-V_F^{-1}\int_{X_y}\varphi_\varepsilon{\omega_y}^d\right),$ and $dd^c_V$ means the differential on the fiber(vertical) direction. Moreover, \[
    \chi^m\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^d=\varepsilon^dh_{\varepsilon,y}\chi^m\wedge{\omega}^d.
    \]
$0\leq \chi\leq \operatorname{tr}_{\omega_\varepsilon}\chi\omega_\varepsilon\leq C\omega_\varepsilon$, $\chi^m\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^d\leq C^m\omega_\varepsilon^n$. Note that $V_\varepsilon\leq C\varepsilon^d$ and $F_\varepsilon\leq C$. Over a compact $f^{-1}(K)\Subset X^\circ$, \[
\omega_\varepsilon^n\leq C\varepsilon^d\Omega\leq C_K\varepsilon^d\chi^m\wedge{\omega}^d.
\]
Hence \[
0<h_{\varepsilon,y}=\frac{\chi^m\wedge\omega_\varepsilon^d}{\varepsilon^d\chi^m\wedge{\omega}^d}\leq \frac{C^m\omega_\varepsilon^n}{\varepsilon^d\chi^m\wedge{\omega}^d}\leq C_K.
\]
Standard $L^\infty$-estimate for complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation gives the desired estimate for $v_{\varepsilon,y}$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md: $\sup_{y\in K}\|v_{\varepsilon,y}-\rho_y\|_{L^\infty}\to 0$, where ${\omega}+dd^c\rho_y$ is the unique Ricci flat metric in class $[{\omega}|_y]$ with $\int_{X_y}\rho_y{\omega_y}^d=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:sharp-schwarz-estimate}, we can choose $0<\delta_\varepsilon\to 0$ such that $\omega_\varepsilon-(1-\delta_\varepsilon)f^*\omega_{\rm can}\geq 0$. Thus \[\begin{aligned}
        \omega_\varepsilon^n\geq&\binom{n}{m}(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^m(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^m\wedge(\omega_{\varepsilon}-(1-\delta_\varepsilon)f^*\omega_{\rm can})^d\\
        =&\binom{n}{m}(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^m(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^{m}\omega_{\varepsilon}^d.
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Let $h_{{\rm RF},y}=\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d/{\omega_y}^d$. Then \[
    \frac{h_{\varepsilon,y}}{h_{{\rm RF},y}}=\frac{(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^m\wedge\omega_\varepsilon
    ^d}{\varepsilon^d(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^m\wedge\omega_{\rm SRF}^d}\leq \frac{\omega_\varepsilon^n}{(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^m\binom{n}{m}\varepsilon^d(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^m\wedge\omega_{\rm SRF}^d}=1+o(1).
    \]
    Here we used that $F_\varepsilon\to f^*\varphi_{\rm can}$ in $L^\infty$ away from singlar fiber(Lemma~\ref{lem:Linfty-density}). 
    Consequently, \[
    0<h_{\varepsilon,y}\leq (1+\eta_{\varepsilon})h_{{\rm RF},y}, \quad \eta_{\varepsilon}\to 0.
    \]
    From stability estimate for complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation, we get the desired $L^\infty$-closeness of the potentials. To see the convergence is uniform on $K$, we sketch a proof here. Set $a=v_{\varepsilon,y}-\rho_y$, and
$\omega_{\varepsilon,y}'=\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}+dd^ca$.
Both forms are positive, $\|a\|_\infty\leq C_K$, and
$(\omega_{\varepsilon,y}')^d/\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d\leq C_K$.
The smooth reference metrics $\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}$ over $K'$ have common
Sobolev and Poincar\'e constants and are uniformly equivalent to
${\omega_y}$. Since $\int a\,{\omega_y}^d=0$, integration by
parts gives
\[
 \begin{split}
\int_{X_y}\sqrt{-1}\partial a\wedge\bar\partial a\wedge\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^{d-1}
&\leq\int_{X_y}\sqrt{-1}\partial a\wedge\bar\partial a
\wedge\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(\omega_{\varepsilon,y}')^j\wedge\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^{d-1-j}\\
&=-\int_{X_y}a((\omega_{\varepsilon,y}')^d-\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d)
\leq C_K\eta_\varepsilon,\\
\|a\|_{L^2(\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d)}&\leq C_K\eta_\varepsilon^{1/2}.
\end{split}
\]
Let $u=a_+$, from difference of two equations we get
\[
 \begin{split}
 (p-1)\int u^{p-2}\sqrt{-1}\partial u\wedge\bar\partial u\wedge\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^{d-1}
 &\leq C_K\int u^{p-1}\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d,\\
 \|u\|_{L^{pq}(\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d)}^p
 &\leq C_Kp^2\int u^{p-1}\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}^d .
 \end{split}
\]
Here $q>1$ is a common fiber Sobolev exponent, and the zero-order
Sobolev term is absorbed using $0\leq u\leq C_K$. Moser iteration gives
\[
 \|u\|_{L^\infty}\leq C_K\|u\|_{L^2}^\beta,\qquad\beta=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{2q^k}{p_k} =\frac{2}{2+q/(q-1)}>0.
\]
Applying this to both signs proves
$\|a\|_{L^\infty}\leq C_K\eta_\varepsilon^{\beta/2}\to0$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
The form
\[
 T_\varepsilon=
 \frac{f_*(\omega_\varepsilon^{d+1}-\varepsilon^{d+1}\omega_{\rm SRF}^{d+1})}{(d+1)\varepsilon^dV_F}
\]
is smooth and closed on $Y^\circ$. For any compact $K\Subset Y^\circ$,  $T_\varepsilon\to \omega_{\rm can}$ uniformly on $K$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As before, choose $0<\delta_\varepsilon\to 0$ such that $\gamma_\varepsilon:=\omega_{\varepsilon}-(1-\delta_\varepsilon)f^*\omega_{\rm can}\geq 0$. Then $R_\varepsilon:=f_*(\gamma_\varepsilon^{d+1})/((d+1)\varepsilon^dV_F)\geq 0$.  \[
\omega_\varepsilon^{d+1}-\gamma_\varepsilon^{d+1}=(1-\delta_\varepsilon)f^*\omega_{\rm can}\sum_{i=0}^{d}\omega_\varepsilon^i\gamma_\varepsilon^{d-i}.
\]
Only products in the fiber direction contribute to the fiber integration, hence \[
f_*(\sum_{i=0}^{d}\omega_\varepsilon^i\gamma_\varepsilon^{d-i})=\int_{X_y}(\omega_{\varepsilon,y})^d=(d+1)V_F\varepsilon^d.
\]
As a result, $T_\varepsilon=(1-\delta_\varepsilon)\omega_{\rm can}+R_\varepsilon-\frac{\varepsilon f_*(\omega_{\rm SRF}^{d+1})}{(d+1)V_F}$.
On the other hand, \[\begin{aligned}
f_*\omega_\varepsilon^n\geq &f_*\left(\binom{n}{d+1}\gamma_\varepsilon^{d+1}(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^{m-1}f^*\omega_{\rm can}^{m-1}+\binom{n}{m}\gamma_\varepsilon^d(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^mf^*\omega_{\rm can}^m\right)\\
=&\binom{n}{d}\varepsilon^dV_F[(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^{m-1}mR_\varepsilon\wedge\omega_{\rm can}^{m-1}+(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^m\omega_{\rm can}^m]
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\[
\frac{f_*\omega_\varepsilon^n}{\binom{n}{m}\varepsilon^d V_F\omega_{\rm can}^m}\geq (1-\delta_\varepsilon)^{m-1}\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_{\rm can}}R_\varepsilon+(1-\delta_\varepsilon)^m.
\]
Since $f_*\omega_\varepsilon^n\to V_{\varepsilon}f^*\omega_{\rm can}^m$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:Linfty-density}, we get \[
0\leq |R_\varepsilon|_{\omega_{\rm can}}\leq \operatorname{tr}_{\omega_{\rm can}}R_\varepsilon\to 0.
\]
This proves $T_\varepsilon\to \omega_{\rm can}$ uniformly away from singular fibers.
head: environment

label: lem:r-varepsilon
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:r-varepsilon}
 There are smooth function $r_\varepsilon$ on $X^\circ$ such that for any compact $K\Subset Y^\circ$\[
    \omega_\varepsilon=f^*T_\varepsilon+\varepsilon\omega_{\rm SRF}+\varepsilondd^c r_\varepsilon \text{ on }X^\circ, \qquad \|r_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(f^{-1}(K))}\to 0. 
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For a potential $\varphi$, recall that the energy is \[
    E_y(\varphi):=\frac{1}{(d+1)V_F}\sum_{j=0}^d\int_{X_y}\varphi({\omega_y}+dd^c\varphi)^j\wedge{\omega_y}^{d-j}.
    \]
    Here and in the following $dd^c$ is taken with respect to the full directions. 
    It follows that \[
    f_*(({\omega}+dd^c\varphi)^{d+1}-{\omega}^{d+1})=(d+1)vV_Fdd^c E_y(\varphi)
    \]
    We can write $\omega_{\varepsilon}=f^*(\chi_Y+dd^c \bar{\varphi}_{\varepsilon,y})+\varepsilon({\omega}+dd^c v_{\varepsilon,y})$, where $\bar{\varphi}_{\varepsilon,y}=V_F^{-1}\int_{X_y}\varphi_{\varepsilon}{\omega_y}^d$.
    Hence \[
 \frac{f_*(\omega_\varepsilon^{d+1})}
      {(d+1)\varepsilon^dV_F}
 =\chi_Y+dd^c\bar{\varphi}_{\varepsilon,y}
   +\frac{\varepsilon f_*(({\omega}+dd^c v_{\varepsilon,y})^{d+1})}
          {(d+1)V_F}.
    \]
    By the definition of $T_\varepsilon$, we get \[
    T_\varepsilon=\chi_Y+dd^c \bar{\varphi}_{\varepsilon,y}+\varepsilondd^c(E_y(v_{\varepsilon,y})-E_{y}(\rho)).
    \]
    Note that \[
    |E_y(v_{\varepsilon,y})-E_y(\rho)|\leq \|v_{\varepsilon,y}-\rho\|_{L^\infty}\to 0.
    \]
    Hence let $r_\varepsilon=v_{\varepsilon,y}-\rho-f^*(E_y(v_{\varepsilon,y})-E_y(\rho))$, we get the desired representation and the estimate.

label: thm:Cheng-Xu.
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Cheng-Xu.}
    Suppose on $B_1\subset\mathbb C^n$ that
\[
 C_0^{-1}\omega_{\rm E}\leq dd^cw_0\leq C_0\omega_{\rm E},
 \qquad\|D^3w_0\|_\infty\leq C_0.
\]
For every $1<P<\infty$, there are tolerances $\delta_0(C_0,n)>0$
and $\delta_{\rm MA}(n,P)>0$ such that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \phi\in C^0\cap\operatorname{PSH}(B_1),\qquad\|\phi-w_0\|_\infty\leq\delta_0,\\
 (1-\delta_{\rm MA})\omega_{\rm E}^n\leq(dd^c\phi)^n\leq(1+\delta_{\rm MA})\omega_{\rm E}^n
 \end{gathered}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|\phi\|_{W^{2,P}(B_{1/2})}\leq C.
\]
head: environment
name: Cheng-Xu, Theorem 1.4

label: lem:metric-convergence
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $d=0$, $f:X^\circ\to Y^\circ$ is biholomorphic.
The sharp Schwarz estimate gives
$\omega_\varepsilon\geq(1-o(1))f^*\omega_{\rm can}$, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:Linfty-density} gives
$\omega_\varepsilon^n/(f^*\omega_{\rm can})^n\to1$.
Every eigenvalue is bounded below by $1-o(1)$ and their product
tends to $1$; hence every eigenvalue tends to $1$.
This proves (1), with the convention $\omega_{\rm SRF}={\omega}$.
The fibers are points, so (2) is immediate. Assume henceforth $d>0$.

Suppose $\varepsilon_j\to 0$, and choose arbitrary $x_j\in f^{-1}(K)$. After passing to subsequence, $x_j\to x_0\in f^{-1}(K)$. We fix a submersion coordinates $(y,z)\in \mathbb C^m\times \mathbb C^d$ around $x_0$, such that $f(y,z)=y$. Suppose $x_j=(y_j,z_j)$. Define on a fixed polydisc centered at zero\[
    D_j(w,\zeta)=(y_j+\sqrt{\varepsilon_j}w,z_j+\zeta), \quad \widetilde{\omega}_j=\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*\omega_{\varepsilon_j}
    \]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:r-varepsilon}, \[
\widetilde{\omega}_j=\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*T_{\varepsilon_j}+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})+dd^c(r_{\varepsilon_j}\circ D_j).
\]
The reference forms converges \[
\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*T_{\varepsilon_j}+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})\to \omega_\infty:=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{\rm can}(y_0)+\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{\rm SRF}|_{X_{y_0}}\quad \text{ in } L^\infty,
\]
where $\operatorname{pr}_1$ is the projection to $y$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2$ is the projection to $z$. 

The previous lemma provides $b_j$ such that \[
dd^c b_j=\varepsilon_{j}^{-1}D_j^*(f^*T_{\varepsilon_j}+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})-\omega_\infty, \quad \|b_j\|_{L^\infty}\to 0.
\]
Fix $w_0$ with $dd^c w_0=\omega_\infty$. Then \[
\phi_j:=w_0+b_j+r_{\varepsilon_j}\circ D_j, \qquad dd^c\phi_j=\widetilde{\omega}_j, \qquad \|\phi_j-w_0\|_{L^\infty}\to 0.
\]
Let $\omega_E=dd^c(|w|^2+|\zeta|^2)$, then we have the volume density convergence \[
\frac{(dd^c\phi_j)^n}{\omega_E^n}=\frac{\varepsilon_j^{-n}D_j^*(\omega_{\varepsilon_j}^n)}{\omega_E^n}\to \frac{\omega_\infty^n}{\omega_E^n}, \quad \text{ in } L^\infty.
\]
Choose $p>3n(n-1)$ and $P>\max\{2n,p,(n-1)p\}$. After a linear change, we can assume $dd^c w_0=\omega_E(0)$. Choose a fixed $r_*>0$ such taht \[
\left|\frac{(dd^c w_0)^n}{\omega_E^n}-1\right|<\frac{1}{2}\delta_{\operatorname{MA}}(n,P) \text{ on }B_{r_*}.
\]
Pull back by dilation $z\mapsto r_*z$ and divide the potentials by
$r_*^2$, retaining their names. The rescaled reference $w_0$ is fixed,
so its ellipticity and third derivatives are bounded by some $C_0$.
Since $r_*$ is fixed, for all
sufficiently large $j$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \|\phi_j-w_0\|_\infty\leq\delta_0(C_0,n),\\
 (1-\delta_{\rm MA}(n,P))\omega_{\rm E}^n
 \leq(dd^c\phi_j)^n
 \leq(1+\delta_{\rm MA}(n,P))\omega_{\rm E}^n.
 \end{gathered}
\]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Cheng-Xu.}, we get $\|\phi_j\|_{W^{2,P}(B_\frac12)}\leq C.$ Note that for any positive $(1,1)$-form $\alpha$, \[
\operatorname{tr}_\alpha\omega_E\leq (\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_E}\alpha)^{n-1}\frac{\omega_E^n}{\alpha^n}.
\]
Let $\alpha=dd^c\phi_j$, then we get\[
\|\operatorname{tr}_{\omega_E}dd^c\phi_j\|_{L^P(B_\frac12)}+\|\operatorname{tr}_{dd^c\phi_j}\omega_E\|_{L^{P/(n-1)}(B_\frac12)}\leq C.
\]
In particular both traces have bounded $L^p$ norm. 
We also have the cscK equation $R(dd^c\phi_j)=r_*^2\varepsilon_j\underline{R}_{\varepsilon_j}$. So $|R(dd^c\phi_j)|+|\phi_j|\leq C$.
Then we can apply Chen-Cheng's local estimate \cite[Section 6]{CC17}, on $B_\frac14$\[
C^{-1}\omega_E\leq dd^c\phi_j\leq C\omega_E, \qquad \|\phi_j\|_{C^k}\leq C_k,
\]for any $k>0$.
Hence we get the smooth convergence $\widetilde{\omega}_j\to \omega_\infty$.

The model $\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*\omega_{\rm can}
+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})$ also converges to $\omega_\infty$.
Moreover, $\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*\omega_{\rm can}
+\varepsilon_j{\omega})$ has a positive smooth limit. Invariance of
relative form norms under pullback and common scaling gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
&\left|\omega_{\varepsilon_j}-(f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})\right|_{f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon_j{\omega}}(x_j)\\
 &\quad=\left|\widetilde{\omega}_j-\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon_j\omega_{\rm SRF})\right|_{\varepsilon_j^{-1}D_j^*(f^*\omega_{\rm can}+\varepsilon_j{\omega})}(0)\longrightarrow0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The centers $x_j$ were arbitrary, so (i) is proved.

Restriction $\omega_\varepsilon$ to a fiber, we have 
$\varepsilon^{-1}\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y}
\leq C_K\omega_{{\rm SRF},y}$. The fixed compact smooth family of
Ricci-flat fibers has uniformly bounded diameters. This proves (ii).

label: lem:ltz-distance
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:ltz-local-input
title: Proof
body_md:
The cited arguments are metric arguments and apply to the present
family with the following inputs. For each $K\Subset Y^\circ$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ltz-local-input}
 \begin{gathered}
 \|\omega_\varepsilon-f^*\omega_{\rm can}\|
       _{C^0(f^{-1}(K),{\omega})}\longrightarrow0,\\
 \sup_{y\in K}\operatorname{diam}(X_y,\omega_\varepsilon|_{X_y})
       \longrightarrow0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounds} gives, with constants independent of
$\varepsilon$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ltz-volume-input}
 \mu_\varepsilon\leq C\Omega,\qquad
 \mu_\varepsilon(B_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,r))\geq C^{-1}r^{a_{\rm vol}}
 \quad(x\in X,\ 0<r<1).
\end{equation}
Since $f^{-1}(D)$ is proper analytic, $\Omega(f^{-1}(D))=0$.
Consequently, for a compact exhaustion $K_j\Subset Y^\circ$,
\[
 \sup_\varepsilon\mu_\varepsilon(X\setminus f^{-1}(K_j))
 \leq C\int_{X\setminus f^{-1}(K_j)}\Omega\longrightarrow0.
\]
Together with the theorem of Szekelyhidi~\ref{thm:completion}, these are the inputs to
\cite[Lemma~4.1]{LTZ26}. The regular path construction in
\cite[Lemma~4.2]{LTZ26} and \eqref{eq:ltz-local-input} give
\cite[equation~(4.14), in the proof of Lemma~4.3]{LTZ26}.
No evolution equation is used in these steps.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:lower-distance}
For $0<m\leq n$,

\sup_{x,x'\in X}
\big(d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))-d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')\big)_+

head: environment

label: prop:distortion
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:u9
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\delta>0$, and choose $K\Subset Y^\circ$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:ltz-distance}\textup{(i)}. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:ltz-distance}\textup{(ii)} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:lower-distance}, for all sufficiently small
$\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(z,z')
 &\leq d_{\rm can}(f(z),f(z'))+\delta
 &&(z,z'\in f^{-1}(K)),\\
 d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))
 &\leq d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')+\delta
 &&(x,x'\in X).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For arbitrary $x,x'\in X$, choose $z,z'\in f^{-1}(K)$ with
\[
d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,z)<\delta,\qquad
d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x',z')<\delta.
\]
The lower distance estimate then gives
\[
 d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(z))<2\delta,\qquad
 d_{\rm can}(f(x'),f(z'))<2\delta.
\]
Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')&\leq2\delta+d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(z,z')\\
&\leq3\delta+d_{\rm can}(f(z),f(z'))\\
&\leq7\delta+d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x')).
 \end{aligned}
\]
First $\varepsilon\to0$, then $\delta\downarrow0$, yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:u9}
 \sup_{x,x'\in X}\bigl(d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')-d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))\bigr)_+\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Combining this with Proposition~\ref{prop:lower-distance} proves
\textup{(i)}. This is the metric reduction of
\cite[Lemma~4.3]{LTZ26}, with the uniform lower estimate also
controlling the endpoints outside $f^{-1}(K)$.

For \textup{(ii)}, the surjectivity of $f$ makes
$\mathcal R_f=\{(x,f(x)):x\in X\}$ a correspondence. Thus
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\rm GH}\bigl((X,d_{\omega_\varepsilon}),(Y,d_{\rm can})\bigr)
 &\leq\tfrac12\operatorname{dis}(\mathcal R_f)\\
 &=\tfrac12\sup_{x,x'\in X}
       |d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')-d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))|
 \longrightarrow0.
 \end{aligned}\qedhere
\]

label: lem:lip-lift-approximation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lip-lift-approximation}
    For any $v\in \operatorname{Lip}(Y,d_{\rm can})$ with $\operatorname{Lip}_{d_{\rm can}}(v)\leq 1$, and any $\delta>0$, there exits smooth functions $v_\varepsilon$ such that $\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}\|v_{\varepsilon}-f^*v\|_{L^\infty}\leq \delta$ and $\operatorname{Lip}_{d_{\omega_{\varepsilon}}}(v_\varepsilon)\leq 1+\delta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\delta>0$ and a finite $\delta$-net $\{z_1,\ldots,z_N\}$ in
$(Y,d_{\rm can})$. For $v_j(z)=d_{\rm can}(z,z_j)$,
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}(v_j)\leq1,\qquad
 d_{\rm can}(z,z')\leq2\delta+\max_j|v_j(z)-v_j(z')|.
\]
Choose $v_{\varepsilon,j}$ from the preceding lemma, 
and set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 a_\varepsilon&=\max_j
       \bigl(\|v_{\varepsilon,j}-f^*v_j\|_\infty-\delta\bigr)_+\to0,\\
 b_\varepsilon&=\max_j
       \bigl(\operatorname{Lip}_{\omega_\varepsilon}(v_{\varepsilon,j})-1-\delta\bigr)_+\to0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For all $x,x'\in X$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))
 &\leq2\delta+\max_j|v_j(f(x))-v_j(f(x'))|\\
 &\leq4\delta+2a_\varepsilon
                +\max_j|v_{\varepsilon,j}(x)-v_{\varepsilon,j}(x')|\\
 &\leq4\delta+2a_\varepsilon
                +(1+\delta+b_\varepsilon)d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x').
 \end{aligned}
\]
Using $\operatorname{diam}(X,\omega_\varepsilon)\leq C$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:bounds},
\[
 \limsup_{\varepsilon\to0}\sup_{x,x'\in X}
 \bigl(d_{\rm can}(f(x),f(x'))-d_{\omega_\varepsilon}(x,x')\bigr)_+
 \leq(4+C)\delta.
\]
Let $\delta\downarrow0$.

label: lem:Resolvent estimate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Resolvent estimate}
Let $h\in W^{1,2}$ be the unique solution to $\Delta h=\lambda h+g$ for $\lambda>0$, and $g\in L^\infty$. Then $\operatorname{Lip}(h)\leq C_\lambda\|g\|_{L^\infty}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Szekelyhidi's theorem shows that the $(Y,d_{m can},
u_{m can})$ is a $RCD(-1,2m)$ space. \cite[Theorem 2.33]{HS26}(see also \cite{JKY14}) shows the quantitative Lipschitz regularity of solution of Poisson equations over balls.  Cover $Y$ by finite balls gives \[
    |
abla h|(x)\leq C(\|h\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Delta h\|_{L^\infty})\leq C_\lambda\|g\|_{L^\infty},
    \] for $
u_{m can}$-almost every $ x$.  Such $h$ has a unique $\operatorname{Lip}$-representative; see the proof of \cite[Proposition 9]{S25RCD}.
head: environment

label: lem:sharp-lip
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sharp-lip}
    For $\lambda>1$ and $g\in \operatorname{Lip}(Y)$. The solution to $\Delta h=\lambda h+g$ satisfies the sharper $\operatorname{Lip}$-bound: \[
    \operatorname{Lip}(h)\leq \frac{1}{\lambda-1/2}\operatorname{Lip}(g).
    \]Moreover, $\|\lambda h+g\|_{L^\infty}\to 0$ as $\lambda\to \infty.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From local regularity, $h\in W^{3,p}_{loc}(Y^\circ)$ for any $p>1$, and hence locally $C^2$. The previous lemma gives $|\nabla h|^2\in L^\infty$. Since $\operatorname{Ric}(\omega_{\rm can})\geq -\omega_{\rm can}$, we have, on $Y^\circ$, \[
    \Delta|\nabla h|_\omega^2\geq \sum_{i,j}(|h_{ij}|^2+|h_{i\bar j}|^2)+(2\lambda-1)|\nabla h|_\omega^2+2\operatorname{Re}h_ig_{\bar i}\geq (2\lambda-1)|\nabla h|_\omega(|\nabla h|_\omega-L),
    \]where we take $L=(2\lambda-1)^{-1}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{Lip}(g)$. 
    Let $w=|\nabla u|_\omega^2$ and $z=(w-L^2)_+$. Test the Bochner formula with $\xi_j^2z$, where $\xi_j$ is the cut-off with capacity tends to $0$. Integration by parts and Young's inequality give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
\int\xi_j^2|\nabla z|_\omega^2
 +(2\lambda-1)\int\xi_j^2z\sqrt w(\sqrt w-L)
 &\leq-\int\xi_jz\langle \nabla \xi_j,\nabla w\rangle\\
 &\leq\frac14\int\xi_j^2|\nabla z|^2
       +\|z\|_\infty^2\int|\nabla\xi_j|^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Absorb the first term on the right. By  Fatou's lemma,
\[
 (\lambda-1)\int z\sqrt w(\sqrt w-L)=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad z=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Lip}(h)\leq\frac{\operatorname{Lip}(g)}{\lambda-1/2}.
\]

For the uniform convergence, test the equation with $\lambda h+g$, we get \[
\|\lambda h+g\|_{L^2}\leq \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\lambda}}\|\nabla g\|_{L^2}\to 0. 
\]
After scaling, assume $\operatorname{Lip}(g)\leq 1$. For $\lambda>2$, $\operatorname{Lip}(\lambda h+g)\leq 3$. Hence if $\|\lambda h+g\|_{L^\infty}\ge a>0$, \[
\|\lambda h+g\|_{L^2}^2\geq \frac{a^2}{4}\inf_{y\in Y}\nu_{\rm can}(B_{d_{\rm can}}(y,a/6))>0.
\]A contradiction.

label: lem:removable
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{lem:removable}For $\lambda>0$, $g\in L^\infty(Y)$, and $h\in C^\infty(Y^\circ)\cap L^\infty(Y^\circ)$, if $h$ satisfies $\Delta h=\lambda h+g$ pointwise on $Y^\circ$, then $h\in W^{1,2}$ and is the weak solution to $\Delta h=\lambda h+g$ on $Y$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi_j$ be the sequence of cut-offs with capacity tends to $0$. Choose test function $\xi_j^2h$, then \[
   \begin{aligned}
\int\xi_j^2|\nabla h|^2+\lambda\int\xi_j^2h^2
 &=-\int g\xi_j^2h-2\int\xi_jh\langle \nabla h,\nabla \xi_j\rangle\\
&\leq\|g\|_{L^\infty}\|h\|_{L^\infty}+\frac12\int\xi_j^2|\nabla h|^2+2\|h\|_{L^\infty}^2\int|\nabla \xi_j|^2.
 \end{aligned}
   \]
   Here all integrals use $d\nu_{\rm can}$, and gradients are taken with respect to the metric $\omega_{\rm can}$.
By Fatou's lemma  $\nabla h\in L^2$. It follows that $h\in W^{1,2}$. The weak equation holds globally by taking limit of test functions in $W^{1,2}$.

label: lem:gradient-estimate-on-total-space
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gradient-estimate-on-total-space}
  Let $\omega$ vary among K\"ahler metrics on $X$ and put
$\mu=\omega^n/\int_X\omega^n$. Suppose, with common constants,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \operatorname{Ric}(\omega)=-\chi-dd^cF,\qquad \chi\geq0,\qquad
 \operatorname{tr}_\omega\chi+|\nabla F|_\omega^2\leq C,\\
 \|a\|_{L^{2q}(\mu)}^2
       \leq C_S\int_X(|\nabla a|_\omega^2+a^2)\,d\mu,\qquad q>1.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Fix $\lambda>0$. If
$\Delta_\omega H=\lambda H+G$ and
$\|G\|_{L^\infty}+\|\nabla G\|_{L^\infty}\leq C$, then
\[
 \|H\|_{L^\infty}+\|\nabla H\|_{L^\infty}\leq C'.
\]
The constant $C'$ depends only on $X,C$ and $\lambda$.
head: environment

label: eq:total-resolvent-energy
title: Proof
body_md:
The maximum principle and the test function $H$ imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:total-resolvent-energy}
\|H\|_\infty\leq\lambda^{-1}\|G\|_\infty,\qquad \int_X(|\nabla H|^2+\lambda H^2)d\mu=-\int_XGHd\mu\leq\lambda^{-1}\|G\|_\infty^2.
\end{equation}
Write $u=|\nabla H|_\omega^2$. At an $\omega$-unitary frame,
with repeated indices summed, the Bochner identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:resolvent-bochner}
 \Delta_\omega u
 =|H_{ij}|^2+|H_{i\bar j}|^2+2\lambda u+2\operatorname{Re}(G_iH_{\bar i})
      -\chi_{i\bar j}H_jH_{\bar i}
      -F_{i\bar j}H_jH_{\bar i}.
\end{equation}
For a nonnegative real test function $\psi$, integration in the
$\bar j$ direction gives the invariant identity
\[
 \begin{split}
 I_\psi&:=\int_X\psi F_{i\bar j}H_jH_{\bar i}\,d\mu\\
 &=-\operatorname{Re}\int_XF_i\bigl(\psi_{\bar j}H_jH_{\bar i}+\psi H_{j\bar j}H_{\bar i} +\psi H_jH_{\bar i\bar j}\bigr)\,d\mu .
 \end{split}
\]
Since $|\nabla F|+|\Delta H|\leq C$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:resolvent-F-term}
 |I_\psi|
 \leq C\int_X\bigl(u|\nabla\psi|+\psi\sqrt u+\psi\sqrt u\,|H_{ij}|\bigr)\,d\mu.
\end{equation}

Put $v=1+u$ and take $\psi=v^{p-1}$, $p\geq2$.
The two terms requiring absorption satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 C(p-1)v^{p-1}|\nabla v|
 &\leq\tfrac{p-1}{4}v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2+Cp\,v^p,\\
 Cv^{p-1/2}|H_{ij}|
 &\leq\tfrac12v^{p-1}|H_{ij}|^2+Cv^p.
 \end{split}
\]
Also $\chi_{i\bar j}H_jH_{\bar i}\leq Cu$ and
$|G_iH_{\bar i}|\leq C\sqrt u$.
Testing \eqref{eq:resolvent-bochner}, using
\eqref{eq:resolvent-F-term}, and retaining the positive Hessian term
therefore gives
\[
 (p-1)\int v^{p-2}|\nabla v|^2
\leq Cp\int v^p,\qquad \int|\nabla v^{p/2}|^2\leq Cp^2\int v^p.
\]
The common Sobolev inequality yields
$\|v\|_{L^{pq}}\leq(Cp^2)^{1/p}\|v\|_{L^p}$.
Iteration with $p=2q^j$ gives $\|v\|_{L^\infty}\leq C\|v\|_{L^2}$.
Finally
\[\|v\|_{L^2}^2\leq\|v\|_{L^\infty}\|v\|_{L^1},\qquad
 \|v\|_{L^1}=1+\int ud\mu\leq C
\]
by \eqref{eq:total-resolvent-energy}. This bounds $\|v\|_{L^\infty}$.

label: lem:gradient-weak-to-sharp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gradient-weak-to-sharp}
Under the hypotheses in the preceding lemma, let $c\geq0$ be fixed and set
$z=(|\nabla H|_\omega^2-c)_+$. Then
\[
 \|z\|_{L^\infty}
 \leq C_c\left(\int_Xz\,d\mu\right)^\alpha,\qquad
 \alpha=\frac{q-1}{3q-1}>0.
\]
In particular, $\int_Xz\,d\mu\to0$ implies $\|z\|_{L^\infty}\to0$.

label: eq:gradient-excess-energy
title: Proof
body_md:
The preceding lemma gives $0\leq u\leq C$ and $0\leq z\leq C$.
Test \eqref{eq:resolvent-bochner} with $\psi=z^{p-1}$, $p\geq3$.
Use regularized positive parts and pass to the limit if necessary.
On $\{z>0\}$, $\nabla z=\nabla u$.
The first term in \eqref{eq:resolvent-F-term} is bounded by
\[
 C(p-1)z^{p-2}|\nabla z|\leq\tfrac{p-1}{4}z^{p-2}|\nabla z|^2+Cp\,z^{p-2}.
\]
The last term is absorbed by
\[
 Cz^{p-1}|H_{ij}|\leq\tfrac12z^{p-1}|H_{ij}|^2+Cz^{p-1}.
\]
All other terms are bounded by $Cz^{p-1}$.
Since $z^{p-1}+z^p\leq C z^{p-2}$ with a constant independent of
$p$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gradient-excess-energy}
 \int_X\bigl(|\nabla z^{p/2}|^2+z^p\bigr)\,d\mu\leq Cp^2\int_Xz^{p-2}\,d\mu.
\end{equation}
Thus
\[
\|z\|_{L^{pq}}\leq(Cp^2)^{1/p}\|z\|_{L^{p-2}}^{(p-2)/p}.
\]
Let $p_0=1$ and $p_{j+1}=q(p_j+2)$. Applying the last inequality
with $p=p_j+2$ gives
\[
 \|z\|_{L^{p_{j+1}}}\leq[C(p_j+2)^2]^{1/(p_j+2)}\|z\|_{L^{p_j}}^{p_j/(p_j+2)}.
\]
Here
\[
p_j=q^j\left(1+\frac{2q}{q-1}\right)-\frac{2q}{q-1},\qquad
 \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{p_j}{p_j+2}=\frac{q^k}{p_k}\longrightarrow\alpha .
\]
The product of the constants is bounded because
$\sum_j\log(C(p_j+2)^2)/(p_j+2)<\infty$.
Letting $k\to\infty$ proves the estimate.
